messages:
Sam (People Ops): Hey team — carrier emailed: dependent add failed due to SSN mismatch (they flagged 3/4 digits as incorrect). I uploaded the docs via secure portal on Friday. Whats the fastest path to correct this and avoid a premium backlog?
Lina (Benefits): Sorry about that. We see the rejection. Carrier usually needs a corrected SSN on their portal + proof (SSN card or SSA printout). Did you include the SSN card in the upload or just the birth cert?
Sam (People Ops): I uploaded birth cert + passport but not SSN card (we were waiting for new card). The employee says the number in Workday might be wrong (typo). How do we fix Workday -> carrier sync?
Samir (Benefits): Quick steps: 1) Ask employee to confirm SSN as they want it entered (screenshot of SSN card or SSA letter preferred). 2) We correct the dependent SSN in Workday and re-run enrollment file to carrier. 3) Mark submission as "SSN correction" in the portal so carrier treats as update not new enrollment. If carrier already created a dependent record with wrong SSN, we need their case ID to merge.
Owen (Payroll): If correction happens mid-month, premiums may have been withheld incorrectly. If carrier backdates coverage and there was an over- or under-collection, payroll will prorate/adjust on next payroll after carrier confirms effective date. If refund required, payroll issues a gross-up or payroll adjustment depending on tax rules.
CarrierBot: Carrier note: Rejections for SSN mismatches require corrected SSN + proof. If corrected SSN is provided within 30 days of original submission, we can amend without rescinding coverage. Provide case ID: CB-752198 to reference.
Sam (People Ops): OK employee will upload SSN card now. Do we also need a signed attestation?
Lina (Benefits): Not usually if SSN card is uploaded, but if card is pending SSA letter plus a signed attestation stating they will provide SSN card within 60 days can work as temporary. But carriers prefer the actual card.
Sam (People Ops): If carrier confirms coverage was active with wrong SSN and later fixes it, will claims be affected? Employee is worried about dentist claim denial already submitted.
Samir (Benefits): Good point. If claim denied due to member ID mismatch, we'll escalate to carrier with the case ID and ask them to reprocess after SSN correction. Collect the claim denial notice and forward to benefits@redwood.com. We'll tag as "urgent - claims impact".
Alex (People Ops): For audit trail, please add a short note in the secure upload ticket with: 1) what changed (SSN typo), 2) who authorized the correction (employee confirmation), and 3) attach denial if any. This helps in tax/reporting and in case of carrier questions.
Owen (Payroll): Also FYI: if we end up refunding premiums, imputed income/tax adjustment may be necessary on that pay. Payroll will coordinate with Tax if gross-up is requested.
Lina (Benefits): Action items for Sam: 1) Have employee upload SSN card to secure portal and include subject: "SSN correction - CB-752198". 2) Forward any claim denial PDFs to benefits@redwood.com. 3) We'll correct Workday SSN and resubmit file. We'll confirm once carrier reprocesses (expect 5-10 business days).
Sam (People Ops): Thanks. I've messaged employee and asked them to upload now. I'll update the portal note with the case ID and the dentist denial PDF if it arrives.
CarrierBot: Carrier expected reprocess ETA: 5 business days after corrected docs.
Sam (People Ops): Appreciate it team :thumbsup:
